The absolute best teacher at UMD. Lectures are clear and straightforward, she fosters an engaging community during office hours, and exams are fair especially with the cheat sheet you are allowed to give. She is very approachable and humble when you ask her any questions, even when they are off topic. More professors need to adopt her attitude.

Opoku is pretty chill. Everyone stops showing up to lectures halfway through as attendance isn't required. Though she does give lots of hints about what questions will be on the test and highlight specific aspects. Her powerpoints are the test and anything on them is fair game. Being in a big lecture hall her microphone isn't loud enough to hear but she does randomly google things relevant to the class which can be interesting but also funny. Ultimately just study the PowerPoint and try your best to go to class. I usually did other work during the time but made sure to listen when she would say test questions.

She is really nice and funny but her class moves very quickly and is hard to stay on top of. I recommend attending lecture as she tells you what problems WILL be on the exam and how to get them right. Her exams aren't necessarily difficult, but the wording and question array will trip you up if you aren't careful. Overall a decent course, just a lot to stay on top of and difficult to keep track of.

She is hard to understand and only puts out study guides for the exams. It would be a little easier if there were more study resources put out because the GSS isn't very helpful. Overall though the class isn't the hardest thing ever.

Professor Goytia is hands down the best professor I've ever had. As a psychology major, I needed to take three additional science/math courses for my degree, so I chose anatomy because it seemed interesting. The content is definitely challenging, but Professor Goytia explains everything thoroughly and takes the time to make sure you truly understand the material. If you’re ever confused, she’s incredibly helpful and supportive.

My lab TA was also amazing, and I’ve heard great things about the other lab sections as well. I enjoyed this class so much that I’m planning to take BSCI202 next!

That said, be prepared to dedicate time—this course is no joke. I practically lived at McKeldin Library studying every day! But if you can fit it into your schedule, I absolutely recommend it.

TAKE HERRRRRRRRR I could not emphasize this more. I loved Dr. Opoku so much I don't understand some of the ratings. She always came in with good energy and made jokes and overall was so nice. During lecture she hinted what was going to be on her exams and her study guides were very helpful as well as the GSS sessions. Overall her exams were straightforward and it was always easy to get above a B. Sometimes her slides can be a bit confusing but just do the study guide and pay attention to what she says in class, going to lectures really helps. I reccommened taking her for BSCI201 and I am so glad that I did.

This course is very content heavy. Opoku is very nice and funny but can be hard to understand. She provides study guides for each exam. Exams are kind of hard because of the multiple choice and T/F so make sure you know your stuff.

Opoku is pretty funny and personable. She posts all content online, including lecture recordings from previous semesters, and even gives out a review sheet before every exam. A big portion of her exams are multiple choice, true/false, and matching that always spells out a phrase. She does have a weird obsession with botox and brings it up at every opportunity. I found the lecture exams very easy as long as you memorize the big ideas and enjoyed having no homework.

Like a lot of other people, I never met Dr. Fox, and I don't know if she's the one responsible for the BSCI201 lab structure. However, the labs themselves are kind of pointless, because you go for multiple hours just to listen to a TA read off slides for you. The lab practicals are a RIDICULOUS amount of information, way more than what you need to know for lecture. For the 2nd lab practical we had to memorize the name, location, origin, insertion, and action of SIXTY FIVE muscles in addition to 3 pages of bone markings and microscopic structure for muscles and bones. It's genuinely not feasible, especially because the practicals were three days after a lecture exam. Since the lecture exams were way easier and also worth more, I just accepted my fate for lab practicals. I also didn't enjoy the lab practical structure. They tape questions to the table and separate them with folders, and you have to spend 2 minutes at each question and rotate 25 times.

Opoku is THE professor you want for BSCI201. she is funny, kind, and VERY knowledgable on the content. her exams have a lot of trick questions BUT if you attend lecture, you will get them all correct because she literally tells you exactly what the questions are going to be and how they will be worded on the exam (multiple times). if you don't attend lecture though, you can still get everything you need from the slideshows, which are all posted on elms. I recommend going to lecture so you can write down the trick questions but even if you don't, if you know the content well enough and read the questions carefully you'll be fine. but tbh go to lecture because she is just the sweetest lady and deserves an audience for her lectures. the course is hard and you will have to study a ton but anatomy is just a dense subject either way.

BSCI201 is the easiest bio course I have ever taken, all of the content was provided in the PowerPoint meaning all you had to do was memorize the information. I did not find the information to be overwhelming as most people said just because each test was usually on 2 or 3 PowerPoints. That being said, the only reason I am getting an A- and not an A is because I failed the first lecture test (37%), but there are 6 tests between lecture and lab as well as a final, and once I figured out a memorization method it wasn't hard to get over 100% on each test because Opoku only tests on what's written on the slides and has plenty of extra credit questions. My only interaction I had with Dr. Opoku outside of lecture was when I went to her office hours after failing the first test and she was very harsh and judgmental, and I left the office in tears. The course is easy, but if you write T and F in the True/False section or tend to make little mistakes/misread directions like that, don't expect sympathy :( Overall, Opoku sets up the course in a way that is easy to succeed, but I would not recommend attending her office hours or interacting with the professor outside of class.
Incredible teacher, gives cheat sheets and extra credit for each assignment. requires a bit of locking in for the practicals but the lecture exams are super chill. highly recommend

Dr Opoku is the GOAT!!!

1. Provides study/review guides for the exams
2. Hosts review sessions the lecture before the exam
3. She will literally tell you what she'll put on the exam
4. A lot of bonus points on exams
5. NO cumulative final exam
6. Power points have all the information you need
7. Recordings of previous lectures are available in the modules

She is my favorite professor I have had so far for a science class. Exams are a bit tricky but you do get a cheat sheet, and there are extra credit points (amount depending on the class average). She truly cares about her students. Yeah, exams might be a little tricky sometimes, but she doesn't fail the entire class and gives us more extra credit points to earn back. She has office hours before and after class, so you can stay after and ask for clarification on tricky subjects. 

Do not underestimate this course though! Be prepared to study a LOT- especially for the lab. Prepare FAR ahead of time in advance of practicals and exams. As long as you do this, you will get an A. Yes, assessments are worth 80% of your grade which seems daunting, but I am 99% sure I am passing this class with an A+. I am not a good test taker either, but you just need to put the time in. 

(if you can't fit Goytia into your schedule and have to take Opoku, I think you will also be fine. I have heard good things about Opoku too. Labs are the exact same for both classes though.)

Dr. Opoku is not only a wonderful lecturer but incredibly organized and WANTS her students to succeed. What is on her slides, you will see on the exams. She also provides study guides for each exam, do these!! BSCI201 is not meant to be an easy course however, if you put in the time you will do great, especially with the help of Dr. Opoku.

Dr. Opoku is to the UMD biology department what Tiger Woods is to the PGA Tour. She is massively over-qualified for her job, and is incredibly well-versed not only in her knowledge of anatomy but also when it comes to writing exams. Very few professors actually base exam questions on what is on their slides, but Dr. Opoku is definitely one of them. I can confidently say that as long as you pay attention in class and take notes on her slides you will do great in her class. If you are studious and willing to put in the work, take her for as many classes as you can. I have had an amazing experience with her not only with BSCI201 but also BSCI447. I cannot recommend her enough but only to those that either have a passion for the subject or are absolute academic weapons. If you are taking this class to fulfill a requirement and don't care much about learning all the content and developing a deep understanding, I'm sure there are easier options out there, so you might have to avoid her. In all other cases, you cannot go wrong with Dr. Opoku

Amazing professor who can actually teach. I took this class in a 6 week summer session and I was able to do it and get the grade I wanted. I won’t lie this was a very fast paced course but if you put in the effort outside of class and take the time to study you can also get the grade you want too. Best professor I took at UMD by far. The lecture exams in this class are not as bad as some people are saying and are very doable. The only issue was the lab exams. Those lab exams had an unreasonable amount of content to learn in a short amount of time. The lab affected my grade the most. I give a 1 star for the lab but a 5+ star for lecture. Like I actually hated the lab with a passion…
Garbage lab. We were expected to know too much information and 70% of the stuff we needed to know wasn’t even tested.
I cant understand her
passing the class is based on the exam, a boring lecturer. For someone who's taught fro a while, teaching skills are clearly lacking.

The main issue I have with this class is the RIDICULOUS amount of knowledge you need to know for each of the lab practicals. In the span of about two weeks, it is expected of you to learn intricate details, most of which you don't even get tested on. At the same time, the allotted 2 hours and 50 minutes is way too long for the "lab," where its just the TA reading off the slides and dumping too much information all at once. This class requires way more memorization than what's actually tested. For example, she expects you to learn over 100 bone markings and over 60 muscles (which you also have to memorize the origin, insertion, and the action for) to answer a total of 25 questions. I also didn't like how the exams were structured, where there were stations with a piece of paper to answer for the most part. Throughout that test, I kept thinking how I could have easily utilized the time better by reviewing other questions and/or moving ahead to the more difficult questions. This "lab" felt more like a glorified lecture with another set of exams rather than applying concepts learned in class to a real-life model. I like BSCI 201 overall, but this "lab" kills the fun of this class.

Honestly is a terrible lab professor. The expected information needed for the lab practicals compared to the lecture is actually terrible. I aced all the lecture exams but am getting a C simply on how terribly structured the lab practicals are. She is also not the least bit understanding and states in the syllabus she will allow you to retake a lab quiz if you miss it once or remake the in class assignment no question asks, but became extremely passive aggressive when I emailed her about it.

I don't know why she has a 3-star rating; it should be like a 1. She's not aware of her class environment and just reads off lectures. She's basically getting paid to talk. DO NOT TAKE THIS DESPICABLE LADY WHO CAN'T TEACH UNLESS YOU WANT TO SUFFER.

These new reviews are unfair. Yes, her lectures are not very thrilling but anatomy is a hard class because it is an information dense class. She tells you what you need to know during lecture and her exams are very similar, if not, identical to her lecture slides. She tells you the trick questions that will show up on the exam in class and then the correct answer to these trick questions. She also provides an exam review sheet that is almost identical to the exams and she goes over the answers in the lecture before the exam. So yes, while BSCI201 is extremely information heavy and it is a memorization based class, she provides you with all the resources you need to succeed in the class. If you know how to study and are willing to put in the effort, you will do great in this class.

Lectures were long because of one meeting per week but were informative. Was always available and helpful when I had questions during lecture or office hours. Exams were difficult but if you study the course material you'll do well due to the similarity between the two.

She's not that bad. She's pretty fair and if you study a certain way you'll be fine. She's an icon/girl boss so theres bonus points and i can tell shes overqualified. Her exams are only based on the slides so thats good. find study tools, make flash cards for active recall, explain content to a 10 year old, something to know the depths of the topics. Pretty much the matching portion of all her exams are easy since there is a theme, a phrase that is spelled so you can guess it along the way even if you dont know the answers. her multiple choice is a bit difficult for me, at least on first exam, but I only studied the review sheet which is wrong. study for at least a week, write her slides down before class because she goes quickly through them in class. One thing is that she has a hard to understand Ghanian accent and communication for the class is difficult, like i dont know where the syllabus is so i only know when our exams are when she mentions them in class like 2 weeks in advance. Throughout her lectures, she'll clarify things, such as "if i say this on the exam, that would be answered false for the true and false portion". Her final is easy, non-cumulative, a study guide that if she puts something on the exam that wasn't on study guide, she'll give points back. iif you do take her, study in depth, more than just the review sheet 2 days before exam, do the slides notes before lecture, and listen to lecture at least when she clarifies something.

The cheat sheet is so clutch for this class in BSCI201. I usually make a Canva sheet in 5.5 font filled with all the topics covered + she gives extra credit for her exams, which has let me have 100% on all three midterms (I scored around a low A every time prior to extra credit). This let me have more time to study for the lab practicals, which I think are harder than the lecture exams because of the overwhelming amount of vocab you have to memorize. The lab is totally doable as long as you spam Quizlet or Anki over and over again FOR ALL THE THINGS LISTED ON THE STUDY GUIDE (yes its going to be a lot but u can do it) Good luck!

Boring class, 3 exams and a final. I will say that her class is manageable and she did make the final pretty fair, however, if you are not ready to spend hours outside of class learning and retaining informatio,n I would not take her. But Opoku is a good person, just not the best lecturer.

Dr. Goytia is definitely one of the best professors I have ever taken and I thoroughly enjoyed this class! She is passionate about the material and her students' comprehension-- she is enthusiastic and always prepared to explain concepts at any time. I am not one to use office hours often, but I would go up to her before class and felt comfortable asking her questions, knowing she would take the time to help me actually understand. 

This course has LOTS of material, but it's structured in a manageable and honestly enjoyable format since Dr. Goytia's slides have various examples and memorization tools. She takes familiar concepts and relates them back to the new material which makes the class very cohesive and tougher concepts easy to understand. 

 Dr. Goytia is an amazing lecturer and provides great study guides, and practice exams-- paired with the lab there are so many tools provided that will help you succeed on practical and lecture exams. I also noticed she has many regulars and previous students visit during her office hours-- she also knew many students by name which demonstrates her passion for teaching. It is clear she has a true impact on her students, and I 1000% recommend taking her for this class!

First off,  sorry for the long reveiw, I just want you to get a full picture of her class and my feelings on it. I will say that anatomy isn’t necessarily a hard class, but a tedious one. Despite my review, if you have to take Goytia, you are not cooked or finished by any means. I just heavily suggest Justicia. I believe that Goytia’s class is very doable; my issue with her is that her exams are not true to her words, and her practice tests are useless. Still do the study guide but remember that they aren’t representative of her exams. She has a very bothersome tendency to make one topic out of the two to three she talks about the dominant thing on the exam, which is usually the most recent topic she discusses. This makes it hard because you wonder why you even bothered learning a topic when she only asks questions on one. She did this very heavily on this year’s final exam, where she only asked about two to three topics out of the ten learned about. Some topics only had one to three questions dedicated to them out of the 78 questions asked. On the final exam, she said there could be images, and there were no images, and seeing the useless study sheets of mine and my colleagues was baffling. The study sheets seem more helpful than they actually are; please do not take this class for that reason alone, because of how inconsistent her exams are—you may end up putting yourself in a hole if you rely on them. She asks too many questions in such a short amount of time; your study sheet should be used only for glancing. Her practice exams give you a false sense of confidence. They are so much easier than the actual exam it’s not funny. Her slides are not that useful—just research the topics on them. Her lectures are boring, and she does not do nearly as good a job as people say she does at breaking up topics. I once asked her a question with a straightforward answer, and she convoluted the answer, making me wonder why I even asked. Sometimes she gives helpful responses, but it’s 50/50. I can’t comment on GSS and its helpfulness. Her extra credit is not as good as Justicia’s (hers are 10–20 points built in). For the first exam out of 50 points, there were 2 points of extra credit; the second exam, I think, was 10 points of extra credit out of 120; the third exam was 140 points and only had 14 points of extra credit. To do well, really be confident in every topic, especially the more recent ones she teaches, and feel comfortable walking in without a study sheet except for any images with answers. She has quizzes that are easy but tedious and help your grade if you do them on time and don’t sacrifice a single point. But these will hurt your grade, despite the dropping of four of them, if you miss them. These are due early in the morning and during weekends, which makes them easier to miss. She does record her lectures, so you don’t have to go to class—just make sure to watch them. Start early with your studying, especially using the study guide. Pay attention to lab a bit more than lectures, as your lab grade is very important. Please study at least one week early for her exams, but more importantly for the practicals, as they are what get some people. P.S. Don’t miss a practical—the lab coordinator is harsher than the TAs. Goytia is nice, but not as great as I feel the reviews below me say she is. I was warned about her by people in person and used these views to sway me. I regret that now, as my friend has an A in Justicia’s class and I have this grade in Maira’s. Justicia is straightforward—what’s on the slides and her study guide is what’s on the exams. She overprepares you for her exams. Everyone left their final exam for Justicia super early, as she didn’t want to stress her students. She’s also funny. Justicia’s main con, in my opinion, is how exam-reliant her class is. If you tend to do very poorly on exams in general, then you should take Maira. Lastly, I want to say that Maira’s exams come much sooner than in other classes, so be prepared for that.

TLDR: Goytia has weak extra credit, a boring class, unevenly distributed exam topics, easier practice exams than the actual exams, sometimes convoluted answers, and you shouldn’t take her class for the cheat sheet. Choose Justicia if you are good at exams and are taking other difficult classes.

Dr. Goytia is an incredible professor, and anyone at UMD who needs to take BSCI201/202 would be lucky to have her. Anatomy and Physiology is difficult in general, but Dr. Goytia offers many resources, a very generous amount of extra credit (which frankly I didn't even need), and a cheat sheet for BSCI201. She has an enthusiasium for teaching that made me look forward to goig to her class. GO TO LECTURE. They are posted in this class and sometimes I would skip but the material sat better with me by going to lecture. The exams were very fair, and even though I hear they are a bit harder than the other professors who teach this course if you go to lecture an put in the work outside of class you will do good and it will set you up for success in 202 or whatever program you are taking this course for. You really do have to put in the work for this class, these are not exams that you can cram for or put everything on the cheat sheet and expect to do well. I strongly suggest following the study schedule that she shows you the first day of lecture. The practice tests were very accurate and helpful. I didn't go to GSS so I really can't speak on that but going to office hours is very helpful, and even doing the GSS worksheets at home. Overall 1000/10 take Dr. Goytia!!

Like someone said before, a lot of these reviews are harsh. Dr. Fox is reachable by email and does care about your learning.  I'm convinced that everyone who rates Dr. Fox poorly does not put in the work that is needed for this course. Yes, there is a lot of memorization. I actually prefer it is this way because I feel way more prepared for professional schooling as someone who wants to work in healthcare. Also, it's an Anatomy and Physiology course... it is going to be a lot of work. The hard part about labs that I think people struggle with is that there are no out of class assignments besides the Pre-Lab assignments. You have to be self-motivated to do well and put in the work. The study guides are helpful, and so are the many many resources on the ELMS page. If you are reading this and planning on taking 201/202, don't be scared, if you get it the mindset it will be bad, it will be bad. Put in the work and tune out other people's negativity and you will be ok.

Dr. Goytia is an absolute pleasure. She is a great lecturer and gives cheat sheets on the exams that make things much better. You are going to have to study so so much for this class, especially the lab, but it is doable. I worked incredibly hard to get the grade I did in this class, so be prepared to spend a lot of time on this. I agree with the other reviews that say 5 stars for the class, 1 star for the lab because it is genuinely 3 hours of the TA reading off of the slides.

Dr. Opoku is a nice professor, she was helping me with the way I was studying realizing that shortcuts won't do the trick. I was studying the wrong way so she helped guide me the right way in studying. She helped me re-learn some of the material that I was stuck on. I earned a C- because I made a comeback on lab practical #3 and the lecture final, scoring the highest on the 3rd lab practical and the lecture final compared to the other exams. I pushed myself towards the end because I knew I could go for it. Overall, her lectures can get funny at times, and exams are straightforward from the slides. However, grading will depend on your TA. Some grade tough. No homework. This class was not easy especially for the lab. I ended up liking the lecture more than the lab.

Honestly, the lab structures are terrible. I ended up passing anatomy 1 with a C- but now have to take anatomy 2 with the same lab. The lab practicals are also RIDICULOUS. They don't even tell you what you need to memorize. All they tell you is to go memorize all the chapters in the lab manual and the slides. COMPLETE waste of time. The bones and muscles was the RIDICULOUS part of this lab, practical was also bad to. 25 questions on all practicals. Lectures were great but you can't escape lab.
Final was super easy. Honestly class is tough but if u already have her just stick with her as she makes up for it at the end.
Not as straightforward as people claimed. Not that informative and lectures are boring.
Not a good teacher, study guides were not representative of exams.

Her study guides are absolutely awful, they are completely inconsistent with bone charts and muscle charts so you don't know which material you should actually study
- some of the diagrams are in like 480p so you it's hard to tell which part the arrow is pointing to
- the whole study guide is a set of empty diagrams and questions but THERE IS NOT KEY to check if your study guide is correct or not
- the diagrams are inconsistent with the ones on the slides
- she wants us to memorize insertions, origins, and actions of each muscle? Ok cool, but at least give us the information so we can study. The info was NOT covered in the slides (only showed us what the definition of each term is and like 1 example) but we need to know all of them, and its super complicated with all the bone markings and stuff
-- she expects you to know material but does not provide the material so you have to go find it, that's not studying, that's teaching yourself

at least the games under each practical are super helpful

the structure of the labs are super boring, the lectures are fine, but the hour worth of lecture we spend just looking at models on our desks is completely useless
